title: Round-robin rolling hotspot
summary: Equal request counts, wildly unequal delivered value. Reading the whole fleet before you route is worse than sampling two of it.

steps.title: Round robin: equal counts, and it ignores load entirely
body: This run is round robin at 70 requests per second. It delivers 17,361 tok/s of goodput, 93.1% attainment, and a first-token p99 of 8,321 ms. Load spread (coefficient of variation) is 0.43.
Round robin is doing exactly what it promises: request counts are equal. It is also the second-worst of the four routing policies measured, because equal counts is not the same as equal load.
steps.look_for: The heatmap under Machine level: rows are not the same colour even though every replica is getting the same number of requests.

steps.title: Power-of-two-choices: sample two, take the lighter
body: Same arrival rate, only the router changed. Power-of-two-choices reaches 18,127 tok/s goodput, 97.0% attainment, and a first-token p99 of 3,859 ms — less than half of round robin's tail. Load spread falls to 0.33.
Sampling two replicas and taking the less loaded bounds herding by construction. It costs one comparison, not a scan of the fleet.
steps.look_for: The heatmap flattening, and the imbalance coefficient of variation dropping from 0.43 toward 0.33.

steps.title: The trap: reading the whole fleet is worse than sampling it
body: Least-requests inspects all 32 replicas and picks the least loaded one — the obvious thing to do. It is 2.6x worse than power-of-two-choices: 6,943 tok/s goodput, 39.4% attainment, first-token p99 of 20,133 ms, load spread 1.27.
Its telemetry snapshot is up to 1.2 seconds old, so every decision in that window sees the same apparently-idle replica and stampedes onto it. Sampling bounds the stampede; a full scan amplifies it.
steps.look_for: Attainment collapsing from 97% to 39% with no change to the offered load, only to which replicas the router is allowed to see at once.

steps.title: Second-order: round robin beats random
body: Random routing gets 16,961 tok/s goodput, 92.2% attainment, first-token p99 8,590 ms, load spread 0.55 — worse than round robin on every column.
Round robin is perfectly even in request count, which is not the right unit, but it is still less lumpy than independent random choice. Evenness in the wrong unit still beats no evenness at all.
steps.look_for: Random's heatmap noisier than round robin's, even though neither looks at load.

steps.title: Throughput barely moves; goodput is the whole story
body: Throughput across all four policies stays in a narrow band, 17,480 to 18,744 tok/s. The work gets done either way; under the worse policies it just arrives too late to count.
Open the A/B view with A = round robin and B = power-of-two-choices to see the same seed, same arrivals, only the routing policy differing.
steps.look_for: The throughput lines nearly overlapping while the goodput lines separate by 2.6x between least-requests and power-of-two-choices.
